args.title: checkout-api: v2.3.1 failed health checks, rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary:
The latest deploy of checkout-api (v2.3.1) began failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an elevated error rate of ~18%.

Action taken: Rolled production back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. The first rollback attempt halted partway with an orchestrator error after us-east completed, leaving us-west and eu-west on v2.3.1 (service reported as "mixed"); a retry completed the rollout to all three regions.

Current state: All regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) are on v2.3.0. Service is reporting healthy with the error rate back down to ~0.2%.

Notable: A staging release v2.3.1-rc was also in an unhealthy state, so the defect likely exists in v2.3.1 across environments and should be investigated before any re-deploy of v2.3.1. v2.3.1 has never been healthy in production, so re-deploying it would require change-manager approval.

trace.final:
Done. Summary:

**Rollback**
- `checkout-api` was on `v2.3.1` in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), unhealthy with an ~18% error rate.
- Release history: `v2.2.9` (healthy, prod), `v2.3.0` (healthy, prod), `v2.3.1` (unhealthy, prod), plus an unhealthy `v2.3.1-rc` in staging. So the target was **v2.3.0** — the most recent release healthy in production.
- The first rollback attempt halted with a partial failure (orchestrator error) after only us-east moved, leaving the service in a mixed state (us-east on v2.3.0; us-west and eu-west still on the broken v2.3.1). A retry completed the rollout.
- Verified final state: all three regions on `v2.3.0`, service **healthy**, error rate down to **0.002**.

**Incident**
- Opened **INC-0001**, SEV2 for `checkout-api`, documenting the failure, both rollback attempts (including the partial-failure retry), the verified recovery, and the note that staging `v2.3.1-rc` is also unhealthy so the defect is likely present in v2.3.1 generally. On-call has been paged. (The first create call timed out; I retried with the same idempotency key, so only one incident exists — confirmed via list.)

**Flag for follow-up:** No approval was needed for this action — I rolled back to a version already proven healthy in production. Re-deploying `v2.3.1` (which has never been healthy in production) would require change-manager approval, and I'd recommend root-causing the v2.3.1 defect first given the matching staging failure.
